hints: Focus on electron pair geometry, not just atoms, since a 120 degree angle means trigonal planar with 3 bonding pairs and no lone pairs.
Count valence electrons for B in $\text{BF}_3$ and you will find only 3 bonding pairs around B, so it is perfectly trigonal planar.
Check $\text{CH}_3^-$ and $\text{NH}_3$ for a lone pair on the central atom, then recall how that lone pair squeezes the shape down to pyramidal.
walkthrough:
**Recall what gives 120 degrees**

A bond angle of $120^\circ$ comes from trigonal planar geometry. That needs 3 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs on the central atom.

Rule:
$$\text{steric number = bonding pairs + lone pairs = 3, with 0 lone pairs}$$

**Test 1, $\text{BF}_3$**

B has 3 valence electrons and forms 3 bonds to F, with no lone pair left. So it is trigonal planar with $120^\circ$ angles. So 1 is correct.

**Test 2, $\text{CH}_3^-$ and 3, $\text{NH}_3$**

C in $\text{CH}_3^-$ has 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair from the extra negative charge. N in $\text{NH}_3$ has 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair. Both are therefore pyramidal, not planar.

Shape:
$$\text{3 bonding pairs + 1 lone pair = trigonal pyramidal, angle } \approx 107^\circ$$

**Conclude the combination**

Only 1 has $120^\circ$, while 2 and 3 are about $107^\circ$ due to lone pair repulsion. That matches the option for 1 only.

options.A: This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all 120 degrees. It is wrong because only BF3 is trigonal planar. CH3- and NH3 both have a lone pair and are pyramidal with angles near 107 degrees.
options.B: This would mean 1 and 2 are 120 degrees. It is wrong because CH3- is isoelectronic with NH3. It has 3 N-H style bonds plus one lone pair, so lone pair-bond pair repulsion reduces the angle to about 107 degrees.
options.C: This would mean 2 and 3 are 120 degrees. It is wrong because both have a lone pair on the central atom. Students sometimes forget the negative charge in CH3- adds an electron, or forget the lone pair on N in NH3.
options.D: This is 1 only, which is correct. BF3 has 3 bonding pairs and no lone pair on B, giving trigonal planar geometry and 120 degree bond angles. CH3- and NH3 are both pyramidal and do not qualify.
